title: Universal Transformer recurrent step Mirror code
hypothesis: A two-parameter affine step-angle code on one shared recurrent block recovers heldout iteration-specific functions with fewer actual bytes than independent per-step maps; compare no-view, explicit time-angle code, and static per-step rank-2 residuals.
mirror_coordinate: theta(t)=alpha+beta*t applied to a hidden channel pair after each recurrent transition
logical_multiplicity: Terminal iteration counts 1 through 6; fit endpoints 1 and 4, audit 2,3,5,6
controls: shared recurrent block with no step view
generic explicit time-angle law with same two scalar coefficients
success_gate: All fresh worlds: Mirror heldout NRMSE <=1e-4 and total payload <=50% independent; Mirror-specific benefit requires >=10% fewer bytes or MACs than a direct control at comparable quality.
failure_gate: Direct time-angle control is an exact equal-byte/equal-compute alias, or Mirror misses frozen quality/bytes gates.
boundaries: Synthetic recurrent mechanism only; no trained Universal Transformer, algorithmic generalization, language NLL, GPU, or capacity evidence.
Teacher is an affine Givens step orbit, favorable to the Mirror code.
mac_contract: A1 proxy includes input projection, each recurrent block, output/effective-map projection and step view; CPU timing includes full heldout-step execution.
